title: Subset-coordinate principal Čech augmentation equals the tuple augmentation on the union
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $V=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$ and $D_S=D(\prod_{j\in S}f_j)$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $K,T$ be complexes of $A$-modules, with degreewise $A$-linear isomorphisms $\sigma_n:K^n\cong\Gamma(V,J^n)$ and $\tau_n:T^n\cong\prod_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\Gamma(D_S,J^{n+1-|S|})$. Assume $\sigma$ identifies the differential of $K$ with the sectionwise differential of $J$, and $\tau$ identifies the differential of $T$ with the signed total formula: at $S$ its vertical term is $(-1)^{|S|-1}d_J$ and its horizontal term is the sum over $j\in S$ of restriction from $D_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, multiplied by $(-1)^{|\{i\in S:i<j\}|}$, with empty deletions zero. All coefficient degrees are transported by their displayed integer equalities. Let $\alpha:K\to T$ be a chain map which under these coordinates is restriction from $V$ on singleton coordinates and zero on all larger subsets. The open inclusion inequalities and degree equalities in the Lean signature specify only the transports in these formulas. Let R be restriction of sheaf modules to V by overFunctor followed by overEquiv V, let J' be its termwise image of J, and let U_i be the preimage of D(f_i) on V.toScheme. After forgetting the A-module scalar actions on K and T and the O(V)-module scalar actions on the tuple augmentation, the arrow alpha is isomorphic to the actual alternating Cech augmentation of J' for U [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. No K-injectivity is assumed, and no cohomology assertion is made.

proof.text: Compose the forgotten sigma components with the explicit canonical restriction-section transport. Its proved coefficient naturality and the source differential hypothesis intertwine the consecutive differentials. The complex shape reduces every required differential relation to this consecutive case; assemble the source chain isomorphism using HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents.

Apply the tuple total coordinate theorem to T and tau, obtaining degreewise isomorphisms and their consecutive differential equations. Assemble the target chain isomorphism using HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents.

Use injectivity of tau to recover alpha(s) as tau inverse of the singleton restriction function. The coordinate theorem augmentation equation then shows that the two assembled complex isomorphisms form a commuting square. Apply Arrow.isoMk′ to construct the claimed arrow isomorphism.
